  CITY COUNCIL

Tuesday, June 9, 2020  7:00 PM  Teleconference

NOTE:  PUBLIC PARTICIPATION INFORMATION
  Pursuant to the Governor's Executive Order N-29-20, City Council Members will be participating via
  teleconference.

  - City Council meeting videos are live-streamed on the City’s website at www.rhe.city and available for
  viewing thereafter, and televised on Cox 33 and Frontier FiOS 38 on Wednesday and Friday following the
  meeting.

  - Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling: (1-669-900-6833) from any phone,
  Meeting ID: 865 0962 0894, Meeting Password: 066081. (Please note you will not have the ability to
  speak using the call-in option from a phone line.)

  - Public correspondence may be emailed to the City Clerk at laurenp@rollinghillsestatesca.gov. Emails
  received before 5:00 p.m. the night of the Council meeting will be forwarded to the City Council for their
  consideration and included as part of the record.

  - Members of the public may comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes &
  Videos” page of the City’s website (www.rhe.city/MeetingAgendas). Once the agenda is published, there
  will be an “eComment” button next to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to
  the City’s SpeakUp page. After you register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda.
  These comments can be seen by the public, will be considered by the Council and become part of the
  record.

  - Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting may join the Zoom meeting by accessing the
  Zoom app from a computer (downloaded at Zoom.com) or tablet or phone (downloaded in the App Store),
  by entering the following credentials: Meeting ID: 865 0962 0894, Meeting Password: 066081
  Members of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the
  following process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand"
  option at the lower portion of your screen. The City Clerk will send you a chat message to identify which
  item on the agenda you would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City's website under Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos at www.rhe.city.

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

3.  ROLL CALL

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

  NONE

5.  CONSENT CALENDAR
  The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority consent of the
  City Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by a member
  prior to the roll call vote. (Items removed for individual consideration will be voted on separately.)

  A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS
  Reading in full of all ordinances and resolutions presented for consideration to the
  City Council will be waived and all such ordinances and resolutions will be read by
  title only.
  B.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF MAY 26, 2020
  Recommendation: Approve as presented.
  Attachments: Draft Minutes

  C.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS OF MAY & JUNE 2020
  Recommendation: Approve warrants 62825 through 62847 in the amount of
  $322,321.17 and Supplemental Warrants 050520 through 050620; 060120; in the
  amount of $103,792.48 for a grand total amount of $426,113.65 with proper audit.
  Attachments: Demands & Warrants

  D.  GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MINUTES OF MAY 20, 2020
  Recommendation: Receive and file.
  Attachments: Draft Minutes

  E.  ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE MINUTES OF JUNE 3, 2020

  Recommendation: Receive and file.
  Attachments: Draft Minutes

6.  PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS
  This is the appropriate time for members of the public to make comments regarding items not listed on this
  agenda. If you would like to address the City Council, please refer to page 1 of the agenda for instructions
  and options to participate in the meeting. Under the State's open meeting law - the Brown Act - no action
  may be taken on any item not on the agenda.

7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

  NONE

8.  NEW BUSINESS

  A.  MCGOWAN  CONSULTING  LLC  PROFESSIONAL  SERVICES
  AGREEMENT FOR MS4 PERMIT CONSULTING SERVICES
  Memorandum from David Wahba, Director of Community Development & Public
  Works
  Recommendation: That the City Council approve Amendment No. 2 to the
  Professional Services Agreement with McGowan Consulting LLC for MS4 Permit
  compliance assistance for FY 2020-21 in an amount not to exceed $84,620.
  Attachments: Staff Report

  B.  PROPOSAL FOR PAVEMENT MANAGEMENT SYSTEM REPORT UPDATE

  Memorandum from David Wahba, Director of Community Development & Public
  Works
  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the attached Task Order for
  Willdan Engineering to prepare a 2020 Pavement Management System (PMS)
  Report Update in the amount of $35,756.
  Attachments: Staff Report

  C.  FINDING OF PUBLIC CONVENIENCE OR NECESSITY TO SELL
  ALCOHOLIC BEVERAGES FOR OFF-SITE CONSUMPTION AT TARGET,
  LOCATED AT 43 PENINSULA CENTER (PA-200087)
  Memorandum from Jeannie Naughton, Planning Manager
  Recommendation: That the City Council adopt Resolution No. 2457, determining that
  the granting of a Type 21 ABC license to Target Corporation for its store located at
  43 Peninsula Center will further the public convenience or necessity.
  Attachments: Staff Report

  D.  MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING WITH CITY OF LOMITA FOR
  THE PLACEMENT OF AUTOMATIC LICENSE PLATE READER CAMERAS
  PLACED ALONG SHARED BORDER
  Memorandum from Jessica Slawson, Administrative Analyst
  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the Memorandum of Understanding
  between the City of Lomita and Rolling Hills Estates for the placement and operation
  of the Automatic License Plate Reader cameras along shared border.
  Attachments: Staff Report

  E.  RESOLUTION  NO. 2458 AND COOPERATION AGREEMENT  FOR
  PARTICIPATION IN THE LOS ANGELES COUNTY DEVELOPMENT
  AUTHORITY’S COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT (CDBG)
  PROGRAM
  Memorandum from David Wahba, Director of Community Development & Public
  Works
  Recommendation: That the City Council approve Resolution No. 2458, approving
  the City’s participation in the Los Angeles County Development Authority’s
  Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) Program and authorize the Mayor to
  sign a Cooperation Agreement with the County of Los Angeles.
  Attachments: Staff Report + Resolution

9.  OLD BUSINESS

  A.  REINTRODUCTION AND FIRST READING OF ORDINANCE NO. 732
  AMENDING AND RESTATING MUNICIPAL CODE CHAPTER 12.24
  (PARK USE REGULATIONS) OF THE ROLLING HILLS ESTATES
  MUNICIPAL CODE
  Memorandum from Alexa Davis, Assistant City Manager
  Recommendation: That the City Council 1) receive any public testimony; and 2)
  reintroduce Ordinance No. 732 for first reading amending and restating Municipal
  Code Chapter 12.24 "Park Use Regulations."
  Attachments: Staff Report + Ordinance

  B.  MONTECILLO FLOCK CAMERA PILOT EXTENSION REQUEST

  Memorandum from Jessica Slawson, Administrative Analyst
  Recommendation: That the Council discuss the matter and direct staff accordingly.
  Attachments: Staff Report

11.  CITY COUNCIL / REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS
  This item provides the opportunity for Members of the City Council to provide information and reports to
  other Members of the City Council and the public on any issues or activities of Council Committees, ad
  hoc committees, regional or state-wide governmental associations, special districts, joint powers
  authorities and the various committees on which Members of the City Council might serve or have an
  interest, which are not otherwise agendized.

  A.  REPORT  ON  ENVIRONMENTAL  ADVISORY  COMMITTEE’S
  CONSIDERATION OF A PROHIBITION OF GASOLINE-POWERED LEAF
  BLOWERS
  Memorandum from Jeannie Naughton, Planning Manager
  Recommendation: Receive and File.
  Attachments: Staff Report

12.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS
  This item provides the opportunity for Members of the City Council to request information on currently
  pending projects and/or issues of public concern, direct that an item be agendized for future consideration
  and/or make announcements of interest to the public.

13.  CLOSED SESSION
  If you would like to address the City Council regarding an item on the Closed Session agenda, please
  contact the City Manager or City Clerk. Any reportable action taken in Closed Session will be reported
  in Open Session.

  A.  CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATORS
